title: [Activity] Install Anaconda, course materials, and create movie recommendations!

cues.en: Welcome to building recommender systems with machine learning and AI.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到「使用機器學習與 AI 建立推薦系統」。

cues.en: You're going to learn the latest research from me, Frank Kane.
cues.zh: 我是 Frank Kane，將帶你認識最新的研究成果。

cues.en: I spent my career at Amazon.com, where I led the development of many of Amazon's recommendation features.
cues.zh: 我的職涯是在 Amazon.com 度過的，曾領導開發 Amazon 的許多推薦功能。

cues.en: In this course, I'll share the real world problems you'll encounter when developing recommender systems and the real world solutions I've learned over the years.
cues.zh: 在這門課中，我會分享開發推薦系統時會遇到的實際問題，以及這些年累積的實務解決方法。

cues.en: Recommender systems are one of the most valuable applications of machine learning today.
cues.zh: 推薦系統是現今最有價值的機器學習應用之一。

cues.en: Amazon attributes over 20% of their revenue to recommendations, and companies like YouTube and Netflix rely on them entirely to allow their users to discover new content.
cues.zh: Amazon 有超過 20% 的營收來自推薦；YouTube、Netflix 等公司更完全仰賴推薦，協助使用者發現新內容。

cues.en: At the end of this course, you'll have hands on experience in applying a wide variety of recommender system techniques to real world user behavior data.
cues.zh: 完成這門課後，你將擁有實作經驗，能將各式各樣的推薦系統技術應用到真實使用者行為資料。

cues.en: You'll be confident when interviewing for positions at the hottest tech employers that depend on these systems, or you'll know how to apply these lucrative techniques for the employer you already have.
cues.zh: 面試那些仰賴推薦系統的熱門科技公司職缺時，你會更有信心；或者，你會知道如何把這些能創造收益的技術用在目前的公司。

cues.en: We'll start off with an overview of how recommender systems are used, and then we'll create our own framework for testing different algorithms on real world movie ratings data.
cues.zh: 我們會先概述推薦系統的用途，再建立自己的框架，以真實電影評分資料測試不同演算法。

cues.en: Together, we'll develop examples of neighborhood based collaborative filtering, content based filtering, model based methods, and deep learning with artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 我們將一起開發鄰域式協同過濾、內容式過濾、模型式方法，以及使用人工神經網路的深度學習範例。

cues.en: You'll learn how to generate recommendations at massive scale in the cloud using TensorFlow.
cues.zh: 你會學習如何使用 TensorFlow，在雲端大規模產生推薦，

cues.en: Amazon's Destiny, AWS SageMaker, and Apache Spark.
cues.zh: 以及 Amazon 的 DSSTNE、AWS SageMaker 和 Apache Spark。

cues.en: We'll also look at in-depth case studies from YouTube and Netflix and learn from those giants as well.
cues.zh: 我們也會深入研究 YouTube 與 Netflix 的案例，向這些業界巨擘學習。

cues.en: The ideal student for this course has some experience in programming, preferably in the Python language.
cues.zh: 這門課適合有程式設計經驗的學生，最好熟悉 Python。

cues.en: We're going to cover a lot of machine learning algorithms.
cues.zh: 我們將介紹許多機器學習演算法。

cues.en: So some background in computer science will be helpful in understanding how those algorithms work.
cues.zh: 因此，具備一些資訊科學背景，會有助於理解這些演算法的運作方式。

cues.en: As long as you've done some programming before, you should be able to pick things up.
cues.zh: 只要以前寫過程式，應該就能跟上。

cues.en: I know you're itching to go hands on and produce some recommendations on your own, so let's dive right in and get all the software and data you need installed.
cues.zh: 我知道你已經迫不及待，想動手產生自己的推薦，所以直接開始，把需要的軟體與資料都安裝好吧。

cues.en: Let's go ahead and press it and see what happens.
cues.zh: 按下它，看看會發生什麼事。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So let's go ahead and open up a test script from our course materials.
cues.zh: 從課程教材開啟一個測試指令碼，

cues.en: And just make sure it works.
cues.zh: 確認它能正常運作。

cues.en: To do that, we're just going to go up to file open and navigate to our course materials.
cues.zh: 到 File、Open，找到課程教材。

cues.en: Remember I put that under documents.
cues.zh: 記得我把它放在「文件」裡，

cues.en: Under materials.
cues.zh: 教材資料夾中。

cues.en: Let's go to getting started and try the getting started py file.
cues.zh: 進入 GettingStarted，試試 GettingStarted.py 檔案。

cues.en: Take a quick look at the code.
cues.zh: 快速看一下程式碼。

cues.en: We'll come back to it later and walk through it all.
cues.zh: 稍後我們會回來逐一說明。

cues.en: But the interesting thing right now is that we're going to be applying a fairly advanced recommender algorithm called Singular Value Decomposition, or SVD, for short, on 100,000 movie ratings with just
cues.zh: 不過現在有趣的是，只用大約

cues.en: about 60 lines of code.
cues.zh: 60 行程式碼，就能對 100,000 筆電影評分套用相當進階的推薦演算法，叫做奇異值分解，簡稱 SVD。

cues.en: How cool is that?
cues.zh: 很酷吧？

cues.en: This isn't necessarily hard from a coding standpoint.
cues.zh: 從寫程式的角度來說，這不一定很難。

cues.en: Hit the green play button and that will kick off the script.
cues.zh: 按綠色播放按鈕，就會執行這個指令碼。

cues.en: It starts by choosing an arbitrary user user number 85.
cues.zh: 它先任意挑選一位使用者，在這個例子中是編號 85，

cues.en: In our case, who we're going to get to know very well.
cues.zh: 我們會逐漸非常熟悉這位使用者。

cues.en: And summarizing the movies that he loved and the movies he hated, so you can get a sense of his tastes.
cues.zh: 它會整理他喜歡和討厭的電影，讓你了解他的喜好。

cues.en: He seems pretty typical.
cues.zh: 他看起來很典型。

cues.en: Someone who likes good action and sci fi movies and hates movies that really miss the mark, like Super Mario Brothers.
cues.zh: 喜歡好看的動作片和科幻片，討厭那些拍得很失敗的電影，例如《超級瑪利歐兄弟》。

cues.en: If you haven't seen that movie, it's pretty painful, especially if you're a Nintendo fan.
cues.zh: 如果你沒看過，那部電影實在很折磨人，尤其是任天堂迷。

cues.en: Next, we run the SVD algorithm on our movie ratings and use the ratings from everyone else to try to find other movies.
cues.zh: 接著，對電影評分執行 SVD 演算法，利用其他所有人的評分，試著找出

cues.en: User 85 might like that he hasn't already seen it.
cues.zh: 使用者 85 可能喜歡、卻還沒看過的其他電影。

cues.en: Came up with some interesting stuff for movies you've heard of, like Star Wars Episode four.
cues.zh: 結果出現一些有意思的電影，包括你聽過的《星際大戰四部曲》。

cues.en: That recommendation makes intuitive sense based on what we know about this user, but it's hard to tell if a movie you've never heard of is a good recommendation or not.
cues.zh: 根據對這位使用者的了解，這個推薦直覺上很合理；不過，沒聽過的電影就很難判斷是不是好推薦。

cues.en: Indeed, you'll learn in this course that just defining what makes a good recommendation is a huge problem.
cues.zh: 事實上，你會在這門課學到，光是定義什麼叫做好的推薦，就是一個大問題。

cues.en: That's really central to the field of recommender systems.
cues.zh: 這也是推薦系統領域的核心問題。

cues.en: And in many ways, building recommender systems is more of an art than a science.
cues.zh: 從許多方面來說，建立推薦系統與其說是科學，更像是一門藝術。

cues.en: You're trying to get inside people's heads and build models of their preferences.
cues.zh: 你要試著理解人們內心，為他們的喜好建立模型。

cues.en: It's a very hard problem, but also a very fun one to solve.
cues.zh: 這個問題非常困難，但解決起來也很有趣。

cues.en: Anyway, congratulations, you just ran your first movie recommendation system using some real movie rating data from real people.
cues.zh: 總之，恭喜你，你剛才已經用真實使用者的真實電影評分資料，執行了第一個電影推薦系統。

cues.en: There's so much more for us to dive into here, so keep going.
cues.zh: 還有許多內容可以深入探索，繼續吧。

cues.en: This is a really interesting field and even after spending over ten years on it myself, it just doesn't get old.
cues.zh: 這個領域非常有趣，即使我自己已經投入超過十年，依然不覺得厭倦。
